rationale: Started 2026-11-10T08:19:02Z; ended 2026-11-10T08:34:20Z (UTC). I did not produce this decision. Every source_fingerprints file re-hashed to its pinned digest, each checked record's text_path re-hashed to its text_sha256, and each quoted text equals the exact char_start:char_end slice of its held file. I read the original in full (15 FR 9177): EO 10195 of Dec. 20, 1950 designates Korea and adjacent waters within stated limits as a combat zone for IRC sec. 22(b)(13) and fixes June 27, 1950 as the commencing date; number, title, date and FR page confirm identity. The held FR text of EO 10585 (20 FR 17, signed Jan. 1, 1955) designates, under IRC 1954 sec. 112(c)(3), January 31, 1955 as of midnight as the date of termination of combatant activities in the zone comprised of the area described in EO 10195, so it reaches the whole designated area; the producer correctly keeps the signing date apart from the designated termination date. The order has no own-terms end, and cruden number searches for EO:10195 and EO:10585 found no revocation, extension or later change of the termination. Status no holds: after the designated termination the designation carries no continuing operative command, and the tax treatment of service within the period is a surviving consequence, as the 2026-10-28 ruling separates an exhausted command from its consequences. Qualifications for the lifecycle record: the statement that EO 10585 is the only later instrument naming the order is incomplete. Held sources also name it in the Combat Duty Pay Act of 1952 (Pub. L. 82-488 title VII sec. 702(f), source-ladder text, adopting its area as the definition of Korea) and in current 26 U.S.C. 112 notes (current-law MENTIONS: an amendments note recording removal of a statutory clause treating June 25, 1950 as the commencing date for the zone designated in EO 10195, and the printed EO 10585 note); the 1989 codification prints EO 10195 as an editorial note under EO 10585. None continues the designation past Jan. 31, 1955, so the status stands, but the statutory June 25, 1950 start and the inclusive or exclusive midnight reading stay open for the interval.
